solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: He is going to and I am, too

definitions.note: a pronoun standing for any man, here a man's name

parts.note: will expresses the future, as in 'he will' meaning 'he is going to'
taken as written, the two words run together

explanation.surface: A puzzling statement that some man is going somewhere and the speaker is coming along too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is going to' reads as travel, but it is the future auxiliary WILL; 'too' and 'and' just link.
explanation.definitionFit: A common male forename is a fair stand-in for 'he', a man.

clue.text: So thought 'Ought to drop by, ourselves'

indicators.note: the word ought is dropped from the word thought, leaving only its first two letters

parts.note: taken as written
the object pronoun for ourselves is us

explanation.surface: A passing thought that someone ought to call by on us.
explanation.walkthrough: THOUGHT without OUGHT leaves TH, and 'by' simply sets US beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean 'in this way' or 'therefore', as in 'it was so arranged'.

clue.text: Parties with buffets

definitions.meaning: informal word for lively celebrations or social gatherings
as a verb, buffets means strikes or batters hard

explanation.surface: Celebrations that come with self-service spreads of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buffets' reads as party food, but it is the verb meaning hits.
explanation.definitionFit: A party is informally a bash, and to buffet is to hit, which is to bash.

clue.text: Feel an affinity for the intelligent? So do I

parts.note: to feel an affinity for something is to like it
the intelligent are the wise, people of good judgement

explanation.surface: Someone admits fondness for clever people, and a friend chimes in agreeing.
explanation.definitionFit: Said in reply, the word means 'the same goes for me', an agreeing echo of the speaker.

clue.text: Just mad about me

parts.note: being crazy about nobody but yourself describes self-absorption; 'mad about' also hints at an eccentric centred on the ego

explanation.surface: A lover's line: you're only crazy about me.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad about' sounds like romance; the joke is that the speaker is infatuated with themself.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wholly absorbed in themselves, thinking of nothing but their own self, fits that description.

clue.text: Goes off for an overhaul

definitions.meaning: to repair to a place is to go off there, as in 'repaired to the bar'
mending work, fixing what is broken

explanation.surface: A machine is sent away to be fully serviced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes off' suggests food spoiling or a machine failing; it is the old verb 'repair', to go.
explanation.definitionFit: Fixing work is an overhaul, and the formal verb 'repair to' means to betake oneself somewhere.

clue.text: Think you said 'Is in a harem,' quite wrongly

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are put together quite wrongly, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a remark about a woman being in a harem was entirely wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: IS and HAREM are rearranged together; 'in a' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch a remark wrongly is to believe the speaker said something they did not.

clue.text: Clamour to get shots showing wild animals

parts.note: a din is a loud clamour or racket
goes are attempts or turns, as in 'have a few shots at it'

explanation.surface: A noisy crowd gets photographs of wildlife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shots' suggests photographs or gunfire; here it means attempts.
explanation.definitionFit: Australia's feral dogs are an example of wild animals.

clue.text: Finding, on looking quickly through the column

definitions.meaning: to run something down is to track it down and find it
scanning a column of figures or print from top to bottom

explanation.surface: Someone finds what they want by skimming a newspaper column.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just joins the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracking down a fugitive means finding them; scanning a list from top to bottom is the other sense.

clue.text: You won't find the flower of the army in it!

definitions.text: You won't find the flower of the army in it!

parts.words: You won't find the flower of the army in it!
parts.note: a building for growing flowers is also slang for a military prison, where the army's best men are not to be found

explanation.surface: A jibe that the army's finest men never end up in a certain place.
explanation.walkthrough: In British army slang the word names a military prison; 'flower' points to greenhouse plants too.
explanation.definitionFit: Army slang for the military jail, holding the worst soldiers rather than the best.

clue.text: Fur ball the animal swallowed

indicators.note: one word swallowed by another goes inside it

parts.note: the animal here is the cat, the household pet
a ball is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A cat swallowed a furball.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal's hairy covering is its pelt or fur.

clue.text: Ticket one's forged and gives to somebody else

parts.note: a pass is a ticket granting entry

indicators.note: the letters of the word are forged, worked into a new shape

parts.note: the letters of the word, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone's ticket is a forgery and gets handed on to another person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forged' turns ONES into ESON.
explanation.definitionFit: Handing something to another person is a phrasal synonym of transmitting it.

clue.text: Why one's burning to take part?

definitions.text: Why one's burning to take part?

parts.words: Why one's burning to take part?
parts.note: 'burning to take part' suggests eagerness, but the fever is a performer's nerves before playing a role

explanation.surface: Asking why someone is so keen to join in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burning' reads as eagerness; the burning is the heat of nervous fever, and 'part' a theatre role.
explanation.definitionFit: Nervous fright before a performance, felt by an actor about to play a part.

clue.text: Go in squiffy again and don't notice

indicators.note: squiffy means slightly drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the prefix re- means again

explanation.surface: Someone goes in tipsy again and nobody notices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squiffy' (British slang for tipsy) rearranges GO IN to IGNO.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay no attention to something is a plain synonym of not noticing it.

clue.text: True card concealed

parts.note: a heart playing card concealed by a hand laid over it pictures the phrase of solemn sincerity

explanation.surface: A card player hides a genuine card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'True' is the definition: a sincere oath. 'card concealed' pictures a hand covering a heart card.
explanation.definitionFit: Swearing something with palm on chest is a gesture of honesty, so the phrase means truly.

clue.text: The rambling rose I planted in, parched? That's ridiculous

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are planted inside the other word, as a rose is planted in soil

parts.note: parched means dry

indicators.note: a rambling rose sprawls, so the letters wander out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener scoffs at planting a rambling rose in parched ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The garden picture hides two signals: 'rambling' scrambles the flower and I, and 'planted in' puts the result inside the parched word. 'The' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A derisory offer is laughably small, deserving scorn, so absurd.

clue.text: Real mess-up by the dope, as usual

parts.note: both dope and gen are slang for information

indicators.note: a mess-up scrambles the letters of the word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A real mess-up caused by an idiot, as so often happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dope' looks like an idiot but means information, GEN; 'mess-up' rearranges REAL to ERAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Widespread and common, as in 'the general rule', means usual.

clue.text: About to urge deserters to return, weaken visibly

indicators.note: the whole combination is made to return, read backwards
the deserters' word goes about, around, the urging word

parts.note: rats are said to desert a sinking ship
to egg on is to urge

explanation.surface: Someone about to call on deserters to come back visibly loses strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'on the point of' but is the container signal; the combined letters, REGGATS, are then turned by 'to return'. Rats proverbially desert a sinking ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To totter or falter on one's feet is to show weakness for all to see.

clue.text: Try again to get her back and are foolish

indicators.note: the word comes back, so it is read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the letters behave foolishly and are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A suitor tries again to win her back, and both look foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns HER into REH; 'foolish' rearranges ARE to EAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A court that hears a case a second time retries it, so a legal sense of trying again.

clue.text: Acted out a silly lie in, requiring tact and diplomacy

indicators.note: the second jumble goes in the first
acted out suggests performing, but out signals the letters are set out differently

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a silly arrangement means the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tricky situation where a silly lie had to be acted out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges ACTED to DCATE; 'silly' makes ELI from LIE, which goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sensitive situation is one needing careful handling, so a synonym describing it.

clue.text: A hole designed to trap rain in monsoon territory

indicators.note: the jumbled letters trap, enclose, another letter
the letters are designed, arranged afresh

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for rain on weather charts

explanation.surface: A pit dug to catch rainwater in a region of heavy seasonal rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' turns A HOLE into LAHOE, and R goes inside. Lahore is a city in Pakistan's Punjab.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pakistani city whose summer rains come with the south Asian monsoon.

clue.text: Said 'It's a time when everyone's travelling, pet'

indicators.note: the word for the busy period is said, spoken rather than written

parts.words: It's a time when everyone's travelling
parts.note: rush hour or high season is peak time

explanation.surface: Someone announces that it's the busy travel season, addressing a loved one as 'pet'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pet' looks like an endearment but is the definition: a Pekingese dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pekingese is a small lap dog kept as a companion animal.

clue.text: Wasn't fooled by the 'Cut the woman in half' trick?

definitions.meaning: to see the truth behind a deception
the stage illusion where a magician cuts through a box holding his assistant

explanation.surface: A spectator was not taken in by the magician's famous trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeing past a lie is one sense; cutting through with a saw is the other.

clue.text: Concluded it's your turn to speak

definitions.meaning: the radio operator's signal handing the conversation across

explanation.surface: Someone finishes speaking and hands the floor to another.
explanation.definitionFit: Something finished is done with, and radio users say the word to end a transmission.

clue.text: Dashes the future prospects of school leavers

definitions.text: the future prospects of school leavers
definitions.meaning: the professions young people go on to pursue

explanation.surface: Something ruins the job chances of young people leaving school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dashes' reads as 'ruins'; it means hurtles.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to rush wildly; working lives are what school leavers look ahead to.

clue.text: Someone stealing something from the nursery

definitions.meaning: stealing here means moving stealthily, as a sneak does
a trailing climbing plant bought from a garden nursery

explanation.surface: A thief taking something from a child's room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stealing' suggests theft but means moving stealthily; 'nursery' is the plant kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A sneak who moves stealthily, and a climbing plant sold by garden centres.
